report:
Brain, right frontal lesion, stereotactic biopsy

Three smear preparations are made from the tissue. They show discohesive large atypical lymphoid cells with scant cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. The paraffin sections of the residual tissue show one piece of tissue comprising sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, disposed around and within vessel walls, in a background of reactive astrocytosis. There are scattered apoptotic bodies and macrophages within the infiltrate. On immunohistochemistry, the atypical cells are positive for CD20 and MUM1 and negative for CD3. The Ki-67 proliferation index is approximately 90 per cent.

BRAIN, right frontal lobe, stereotactic biopsy - MALIGNANT LYMPHOMA, large B-cell type

The diagnosis should be correlated with flow cytometry, cerebrospinal fluid examination and staging investigations.

Corticosteroid therapy before biopsy may obscure a lymphoid infiltrate; a repeat biopsy should be considered if the clinical and radiological picture is unchanged.
